title: subnet-aware-terraform-registry-seeder + signed-OCI-index and optional kernel-mod bundling
author: Priya Nair
body:
Motivation: Customers operating in constrained on-prem networks often need deterministic local registries seeded into specific subnets (DMZ vs internal, control-plane vs worker-only networks) and a portable, verifiable artifact that can be shipped via offline media. Existing seeding tooling assumes a flat seed node topology and does not provide native signed artifact indexes, nor a safe packaging option for optional host kernel modules (e.g., for BPF/CNI acceleration) that some customers require during install.

This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: 1) a Terraform module (terraform/registry-seeder) that deploys a small, HA local registry cluster seeded atomically with an immutable, signed OCI index and content manifests; the module supports subnet affinity for seed replicas and automatic DNS/HA proxy wiring for restricted networks; 2) an offline bundler that emits a self-validating OCI index (index.json + detached signatures) with optional kernel-module tarball packaging and preflight metadata so air-gapped sites can verify artifacts before bootstrapping.

What changed (high-level):
- New terraform module: terraform/modules/registry-seeder with examples for baremetal (netplan-based host selection), vSphere, and AWS VPC (for hybrid customers); supports seed placement policies: control-plane-only, worker-only, hybrid, and explicit hostlist.
- Registry seeder supports three seeding strategies: push-from-local (preferred for airgap), pull-and-cache (for semi-restricted egress), and redirected manifests (OCI manifest lists rewritten with registryLocation redirects).
- Offline bundler: tooling/bin/oci-seed-bundler.go and a shim script tools/bundle-to-registry.sh to produce a signed index (cosign signatures detached) and a content manifest that includes signed digests for kernel modules and package lists.
- Preflight checks: installer/cli/preflight now validates signatures, verifies digest checksums, and checks host kernel compatibility if kernel-module bundle is present.
- Documentation: docs/airgap/registry-seeding.md + quickstart examples for subnet affinity and deterministic rollback.

Design notes:
- Index signing uses cosign detached signatures (customers can swap to their KMS/HSM) and the bundler records the original source digests to enable deterministic verification after any manifest rewrite during network promotion.
- Seed placement uses Terraform providers and a small placement controller (stateless plan that renders host selection via tags or netplan metadata). We avoid long-lived controllers inside customer clusters to keep the footprint minimal for high-security environments.
- Rollback: seeder deploys content under hashed namespace prefixes and keeps the last two active namespaces; promoter scripts swap DNS and HA proxy targets atomically to rollback.

Testing and validation performed:
- Local integration tests using kind+registry-proxy validating redirectable manifests and cosign verification (tools/test/integration/oci_seeder_test.sh).
- Airgap validation in lab using RKE2 minimal cluster with a 3-node seed placement (control-plane-only) and kernel-module package applied on worker nodes. Digest verification and signature checks exercised.
- Terraform unit tests (tftest) for module inputs/outputs and plan idempotency.

Checklist (what I did):
- [x] Implement terraform module and examples.
- [x] Implement bundler and signature workflow (cosign-based).
- [x] Add preflight validations to installer CLI.
- [x] Add docs and quickstart.
- [x] Integration tests and CI job.

Deployment notes:
- Default behavior is opt-in: kernel-module bundle is disabled by default. To enable, set enable_kernel_modules = true and provide module_kvstore (pre-signed tarball) and host_selector.
- For strict airgap sites, run tools/bundle-to-registry.sh -> copy artifacts to USB or local mirror -> run terraform module with seed_method = "push-from-local".

Rollback and upgrade story:
- Upgrades publish a new hashed namespace (e.g., seeder/sha256-<release>) and seeder keeps previous namespace for quick rollback. Promotion is an atomic DNS/HA proxy swap.
- If a kernel module fails compatibility check during preflight, the installer will abort with a clear remediation path (revert to previous namespace or skip kernel module step).

Related work: ENG-1429 (registry seeding initiative), INF-278 (airgap signature standard).

Notes for reviewers: focus on Terraform module input surface for host selection and the security assumptions around detached cosign signatures. The preflight dependency list and error messages are intentionally explicit to reduce operator ambiguity.

feat(preflight): validate cosign signatures and optional kernel module compatibility
docs: add registry-seeding quickstart and rollback guide
test: add integration test harness for redirectable manifests
chore: add CI workflow for bundler and terraform tftest
review_comments: Marcus Lee: Please make the host_selector schema explicit in the README and add an example for netplan tag-based selection.
Priya Nair: Added netplan selection example and extended README; clarified host_selector precedence rules.
Jamal Rivera: Security nit: use detached signatures by default but allow cosign keyless verification mode via a flag. Also, please ensure the bundler exits non-zero on signature mismatch.
Priya Nair: Implemented keyless verification toggle and explicit exit codes for signature failures. CI tests updated to cover mismatch flows.
Hannah Park: Terraform plan looked good; suggest an output that exposes the active namespace and previous namespace for easier monitoring.
Priya Nair: Added seeder_active_namespace and seeder_previous_namespace outputs.
release_notes: Add terraform registry-seeder module with subnet-aware seed placement and examples for baremetal/vsphere/aws hybrid usage.
Add offline bundler that emits a cosign-signed OCI index and optional kernel-module packaging for air-gapped installs.
Preflight now verifies detached signatures and kernel-module compatibility; rollback via atomic DNS swap supported.
